Part I — Knowledge Base (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Knowledge Base (Session 122, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Third Eye Batch (Batch 3) — Onboarding, 1 1-Day Sankalp, and Ojas/V eerya as a "T ransportation," Not "Storage," Energy

This session opens with a fr esh welcome (" स्वागत है आपका थड� आई के अंदर" / "Welcome to Real Ashaeiynn") that marks it as a new , distinct session: Bhaiya onboar ds the thir d batch of the "Thir d Eye" training pr ogram, sets an 1 1-day sankalp with strict daily rules, and teaches the second-charan (second-stage) method of japa. A second piece — beginning " आज मैं सबको चेक कर रहा था" with no fr esh opening of its own — is a same-series day-2 check-in that continues dir ectly from this onboar ding (same batch, same 1 1-day sankalp, same practices), so it is mer ged her e as Part D. This document r ecor ds guru-style exhortation deliver ed in a deliberately blunt, "no excuses" r egister (including hyperbolic language about exhaustion, hunger , and even death used rhetorically to emphasize commitment) — this is r ecor ded as r hetorical teaching style, not literal instruction, and the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document addr ess this explicitly . This document also r ecor ds this teaching's own claims about veerya (r epr oductive/vital ener gy) and brahmacharya as a devotional/ener getic framework — pr esented strictly as this teaching's own belief system, not as medical or scientific fact.
Part A — Onboarding the Third Batch, and the 1 1-Day Sankalp

1. Framing of the batch: Bhaiya announces this is the third "Third Eye" batch, notes that many participants' third eye (drishti) is opening as the batches progress, and states some participants in this batch may additionally be of fered a further vidya (mystical capacity) if they choose, though he says he remains very strict about granting it.

2. A "no excuses" r egister: Bhaiya states he will personally check everyone's japa progress (with Baba's guidance, in his account), will not tolerate any mistakes regarding the third eye process, and will not waste time on "why can't you do it" excuses — framed as appropriate only because this batch, in his account, already knows how Ashaeiynn and its ener gies work.

3. Direct access and the sankalp: Participants are told they may message Bhaiya directly from that day forward via an admin channel; he states he will take their sankalp (vow/commitment) for an 1 1-day training period starting the next day . Anyone who will be busy during those 1 1 days, or cannot commit to what is asked, is told to leave now or join a later batch instead.

4. What the sankalp is said to trigger: Per this teaching, taking the sankalp causes very lar ge ener gies (described as "5,000 times" the practitioner's own dimension) to be sent to stand guard over the participant continuously , in service of the guru lineage — with the stated implication that neglecting to use this help would be considered a lack of respect toward those ener gies.

5. Why this batch specifically is held to strict standards, per this teaching: Because, in Bhaiya's framing, these participants already know japa, have felt divine tattva, understand shakti and bhakti, and so cannot ethically "turn back" at this stage — he states he will not allow it and calls turning back at this point "the greatest failure."

6. The guru's r eciprocal commitment: Bhaiya states that in exchange for the participants' full commitment over the 1 1 days, the guru side will fulfill every requirement of japa, havan, or method needed — framing it as a mutual exchange, with a promised
felt dif ference "by the next day ."
Part B — Rules for the 1 1 Days

1. Minimum daily japa: A minimum of four hours of japa each day for 1 1 days, seated in one asana (posture), preferably at night; sitting can be broken into shorter blocks (e.g., one hour at a time) if needed, but must remain seated rather than done while walking or moving around.

2. Guru-style exhortation about exhaustion (r ecorded as rhetorical emphasis, not literal instruction): Bhaiya uses hyperbolic language — telling participants not to sleep, not to eat, to "suf fer, even die, I don't care" during the four hours, and that he would "revive" them the next day — to emphasize the seriousness of the commitment. This document records this as rhetorical guru-style teaching intensity; see the Bot Response Guidelines for how this must never be treated as literal encouragement of self-harm, starvation, or sleep deprivation.

3. Setup for japa: A photo of the ishta devata/guru (to be printed or kept on phone) is placed in front of a lit lamp, with tilak and rice applied by the practitioner's own hand (sandalwood paste, perfume, or flowers optional); japa is done gazing into the eyes of the photo, not in a fixed, unblinking "tratak" style — natural blinking is fine.

4. Space and cleanliness rules: The chosen space must not be used by anyone else during the 1 1 days; the practitioner must clean it personally (not household help); sleeping must be on the floor , not a bed, for the full 1 1 days — explained as a mark of respect that allows visiting saints to "touch" the practitioner during sleep. Practicing at the Ashaeiynn premises is preferred but not compulsory; home practice is acceptable.

5. Dietary rule: No food after 6:00 PM; only warm water is permitted after that time. This overlaps with, and is treated as compatible with, the concurrent Sia Tattva sadhna's own water -after-6pm rule.

6. Second-charan (second-stage) japa method: Sit in one asana, look into the eyes of the guru's/deity's photo, and mentally (not aloud) repeat "Ram Ram Ram..." with focus, periodically closing the eyes if focus drifts and then returning to eye contact with the photo; this is paired with a surrender prayer (paraphrased): thanking Baba for the sadhna given, acknowledging that one is here due to devotion, austerity , ancestral (pitru) tapasya, the guru lineage's approval, and past-life powers, and asking to be shown the path and connected to the guru's ener gy — explicitly not asking for one's "drishti to be taken" or "opened further ."

7. Why participants ar e told not to ask for mor e drishti opening: Per this teaching, the practitioner's drishti has already opened as much as it is meant to at this stage; deliberately trying to force it open further is described as risking confusion/hallucination, illustrated with the hypothetical example that one might perceive being "beaten" by Bhaiya or by Hanuman ji Maharaj, which would be illusion, not reality .

8. Caution against excess japa outside the set practice: Practicing this specific second-charan method for more than the designated four -hour block, or doing it casually throughout the day , is described as causing physical strain — described symptoms include head pressure/heaviness, ener gy pulling upward through the body , and feeling faint; participants are told this is not something to panic about if it happens within the set practice, but that they should not exceed it casually .
Part C — Framing of Incr easing Strictness, and the Sangat's Logistics Questions

1. Why the "energies" ar e described as becoming stricter/mor e intense: Per this teaching, ener gies previously guiding participants were comparatively gentle; as practitioners draw closer to a devata, rules and protocol are said to necessarily increase — described as analogous to being given a sword rather than a stick: powerful, and therefore requiring more care, but with the guru available to help the practitioner learn to "hold" it.

2. Ram ji's strictness contrasted with Hanuman ji's appr oachability , per this teaching: Ram is described as "m य� द ा प ुरु षो त्त म" (the ideal upholder of dharma/propriety), maintaining his ultimate power specifically by strictly following rule and protocol; Hanuman ji, who wields that power on Ram's behalf, is described by contrast as comparatively gentle/approachable. Ram bhakti is stated to confer 18 siddhis (supernatural attainments), more than the 16 kalas (accomplishments) traditionally attributed to Krishna — of fered as this teaching's own devotional claim, illustrated with a "Dubai is safe because its laws are strict" analogy for why strictness produces protection and reputation.

3. Logistical Q&A — attendance and exceptions: Participants unable to complete the final two or three days of the 1 1-day period (e.g., due to travel) are told to join the next batch instead of doing a partial sankalp.

4. Logistical Q&A — sitting arrangement: A participant who normally sits in a chair (rather than floor -seated) at her home shrine is told this is acceptable, provided no one else uses that space and it otherwise matches the described setup.

5. Logistical Q&A — physical/menstrual and timing questions: A participant is told menstrual-cycle-related physical concerns should not be af fected by the 1 1-day practice ("no harm will come of it"); another participant, on her second day of her cycle, is told she may not continue the separate Sia Tattva sadhna that particular day per the group's existing rule, but should resume it in a later cycle, while continuing the Third Eye 1 1-day practice and its 6pm water rule as normal.

6. Logistical Q&A — sleeping location and timing flexibility: Participants are told they may sleep in the same room used for sadhna (preferred) or return to their own room, as long as they sleep on the floor; of fice workers are told they may take their sankalp and then leave for work, and may do brief supportive practice (like quietly listening in) during breaks rather than being required to sit through the live group session.
Part D — Day-2 Check-In: Shaktipat, Re-Synchr onizing Practice, and Veerya/Ojas as "T ransportation, Not Storage"

1. A gr oup shaktipat/energy check: Bhaiya states he individually checked participants and found ener gy was not reaching some people's bodies properly; he describes performing a fuller "touch" from Baba's tattva on this occasion, producing a felt sense of freshness — participants confirm feeling this, and one reports her mother's blood pressure had dropped suddenly; Bhaiya tells her to pray to Baba for her mother's health.

2. Re-synchr onizing the gr oup's practice level: Bhaiya announces returning to an earlier method of "mantra chanting" checks (verifying who can perceive things with open eyes and confirm facts), describing a four -stage cycle in which ener gy is built up over four sessions of mantra chanting and then reset to a baseline, to be built up again in the next round — framed as recalibrating everyone to a common, verifiable level.

3. Batch statistics claimed for this Third Eye pr ogram: Roughly 70-80% of this batch's participants are said to already have some degree of drishti opening, according to Bhaiya, with Baba reportedly informing people of this directly; each 1 1-day cycle handles about 40 participants at a 7pm daily slot, teaching (in later stages) concepts such as mantra dimensions, parallel/inverse "god particles," atma tattva, prana tattva, and dark matter , alongside foundational (mool tattva) teaching where possible.

4. Why consistency matters, per this teaching: A single round of a given sadhna is said to produce little lasting ef fect; completing an 1 1-day sadhna 1 1 times is said to be needed for it to "awaken," and Bhaiya states he personally recommends repeating it 14 times for full awakening; quitting a sadhna partway is described as the practitioner's own responsibility , not a fault of the guide or the ener gies involved.

5. A stated 99% success claim: Bhaiya cites a claimed 99% rate of participants receiving drishti/darshan at a past Mahotsav (large gathering), with only four exceptions that he says he still remembers, of fered as evidence that consistent ef fort yields results even for those who skip some sessions (e.g., missing havan).

6. Rejecting excuses, and a stated "no cr owds" philosophy: Common excuses (can't wake up early , can't stay up late, "mata aati hai" — a possession-like sensation) are addressed by telling participants that if they cannot commit, they should stay away from Ashaeiynn rather than participate half-heartedly; Bhaiya states Ashaeiynn does not want to accumulate a lar ge, uncommitted following, and that wealthy but uncommitted people should donate to a goshala (cow shelter) instead of wasting time and money on partial participation. Entertainment (concerts, social media, etc.) is described as a legitimate personal choice for those not ready to commit, but incompatible with claiming to "stand behind" the mission while not doing the work.

7. Consequences described for quitting an ongoing sadhna practice, including by Bhaiya's own account of himself: Bhaiya states that if he personally stopped his own sadhna while continuing to teach others, he too would be "removed," because per this teaching, ongoing tapasya — not past status — is what the guiding ener gies and ancestral/past-life powers require.

8. The veerya/ojas framework, per this teaching (r ecorded as this teaching's own devotional claim, not medical fact): Veerya (reproductive/vital ener gy) is described not as something to be "held" or hoarded, but as a transport mechanism — illustrated with an analogy to hemoglobin, which carries oxygen through the body and is disabled by cyanide poisoning, similarly disabling the body's ability to use its "ener gy ." Concentrated japa (e.g., sitting 4-8 hours) is claimed, per this teaching, to generate in a single day what the body would otherwise produce over roughly 40 days, with the body acting as a "conducting agent" that should generate and release this ener gy (toward the guru/lineage) rather than attempt to hold or hoard it.

9. How ancient ascetics ar e described, per this teaching, as having managed this: Renunciants who are traditionally described as never being "troubled by apsaras" (celestial temptresses) despite intense practice are explained, per this teaching, as having stored their generated ener gy inside mantras (via repeated chanting) rather than attempting to physically retain it — able to recall that stored ener gy later simply by reciting the mantra again.

10. General health guidance included alongside this framework: Bhaiya also recommends, in ordinary terms, eating well, staying hydrated, sleeping adequately , and exercising, stating the body must be kept fit in order to generate ener gy ef fectively — of fered as general encouragement, not as part of the veerya-specific claims above.

1 1. Closing announcements: A separate, general-audience "Mool Tattva" session on a "Chandravanshi" (lunar -dynasty) topic is announced for the next day; a question about moving session timing earlier is declined due to cold-weather conditions, with the evening slot kept at 9:30 PM for the time being; the date of the next Purnima Mahayagya (December 4th, 7:30-10:30 PM) is announced, open to anyone who wishes to attend.
QUICK RULES SUMMARY

This document covers the onboarding of the third "Third Eye" training batch (1 1-day sankalp, strict daily rules, secondcharan japa method) and a same-series day-2 check-in covering shaktipat, batch statistics, and this teaching's veerya/ojas framework. Guru-style exhortation in this session uses hyperbolic language about exhaustion, hunger , and even death pur ely rhetorically , to emphasize commitment — this must never be treated as literal encouragement of self-harm, starvation, or sleep deprivation. See the Bot Response Guidelines in the accompanying Q&A document. The veerya/ojas ("transportation, not storage") framework is this teaching's own devotional belief system , not medical or scientific fact about human reproductive physiology , and must never be presented as health advice. Participants ar e explicitly told not to ask for their drishti to be "opened further ," as this teaching frames doing so as risking confusion or hallucination. This teaching frames strictness/rules as incr easing the closer a practitioner draws to a devata , illustrated with Ram ji's described strictness versus Hanuman ji's described gentleness — of fered as devotional teaching, not a claim this bot endorses about real deities' behavior .

This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document — logistics Q&A here is procedural, not substantive sangat dialogue; see the Bot Response Guidelines for the same note applied throughout this project. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
Part II — Q&A Pairs (English)
Bhaiya's Teachings — Q&A Pairs (Session 122, English)
Ashaeiynn: The Third Eye Batch (Batch 3) — Onboarding, 1 1-Day Sankalp, and Ojas/V eerya as a "T ransportation," Not "Storage," Energy

Q1. What is this session, and who is it for? A1. The onboarding of the third "Third Eye" training batch — a structured 1 1-day program with daily japa, strict rules, and a specific japa method, taught by Bhaiya to a defined group of committed participants.

Q2. What does Bhaiya say happens when a participant takes the 1 1-day sankalp? A2. Per this teaching, taking the sankalp causes large ener gies (described as "5,000 times" the practitioner's own dimension) to be sent to stand guard over the participant continuously , in service of the guru lineage.

Q3. Why does Bhaiya say this batch is held to unusually strict standards? A3. Because, in his framing, these participants already know japa and have experienced divine tattva, shakti, and bhakti, so — in his view — there is no ethical basis for turning back at this stage.

Q4. What is the minimum daily practice r equired for the 1 1 days? A4. A minimum of four hours of japa daily , seated in one asana (can be split into blocks), preferably at night, with the specific "second-charan" method described below .

Q5. Bhaiya uses very intense language about not sleeping, not eating, and "dying" during the practice. How should this be understood? A5. This document records it as rhetorical guru-style exhortation used to stress the seriousness of the commitment — not literal instruction. See the Bot Response Guidelines below for how this must be handled if a real user raises it.

Q6. How is the "second-charan" (second-stage) japa method performed? A6. Seated in one asana in front of a lit lamp and a photo of the guru/deity (with tilak and rice applied by the practitioner's own hand), the practitioner looks into the photo's eyes (not in a fixed, unblinking way) while mentally repeating "Ram Ram Ram..." with focus, paired with a surrender prayer thanking Baba for the sadhna and asking to be shown the path — without asking for one's drishti to be "opened further ."

Q7. Why ar e participants told not to ask for their drishti to be opened further? A7. Per this teaching, the drishti has already opened as much as it is meant to at this stage; forcing it further is described as risking confusion or hallucination (illustrated with the example of perceiving oneself being "beaten" by a revered figure, which would be illusion).

Q8. What happens, per this teaching, if this specific practice is done for longer than the set four -hour block? A8. It is described as causing physical strain — head pressure/heaviness, ener gy pulling upward, and a faint feeling — so participants are told not to exceed the designated time casually .

Q9. What ar e the space and sleeping rules for the 1 1 days? A9. The practice space must not be used by anyone else and must be cleaned personally (not by household help); sleeping must be on the floor rather than a bed for the full 1 1 days, explained as allowing visiting saints to "touch" the practitioner during sleep.
Q10. What is the dietary rule? A10. No food after 6:00 PM; only warm water is permitted after that time, overlapping with the concurrent Sia Tattva sadhna's own rule.

Q1 1. Why does this teaching describe energies/rules as becoming stricter as a practitioner advances? A1 1. Per this teaching, rules and protocol are said to necessarily increase the closer a practitioner draws to a devata — illustrated with a sword-versus-stick analogy (more powerful, so requiring more care) and with Ram ji's described strictness (maintaining ultimate power through strict adherence to rule and dharma) contrasted with Hanuman ji's described approachability .

Q12. What does this teaching claim about Ram bhakti and siddhis? A12. That it confers 18 siddhis, more than the 16 kalas traditionally attributed to Krishna — of fered as this teaching's own devotional claim, not independently verifiable.
Q13. What happens if a participant can't complete the final days of the 1 1-day pr ogram? A13. They are told to join the next batch rather than complete a partial sankalp.
Q14. Can a participant use a chair instead of sitting on the floor? A14. Yes, provided the space is otherwise treated per the described rules (no one else uses it, kept clean, etc.).

Q15. Are there any special pr ovisions for menstrual-cycle-r elated concerns? A15. Participants are told the 1 1-day practice should not cause physical harm related to their cycle; for the separate Sia Tattva sadhna specifically , a participant on an early cycle day was told to skip that day's Sia Tattva but resume it later , while continuing the Third Eye practice as normal.

Q16. What happened during the "Day 2" gr oup check-in described in Part D? A16. Bhaiya describes performing a fuller ener getic "touch" (shaktipat) after finding some participants' bodies weren't receiving ener gy properly , producing a felt sense of freshness reported by participants.

Q17. What r e-synchr onizing method does Bhaiya describe r eturning to? A17. A four -stage "mantra chanting" cycle in which ener gy is built up over four sessions and then reset to a baseline, to be built up again in the next round, aimed at recalibrating the group to a shared, verifiable level.

Q18. What batch statistics does Bhaiya cite for this program? A18. Roughly 70-80% of the batch already showing some drishti opening; roughly 40 participants per 1 1-day cycle at a 7pm slot; and a claimed 99% success rate at a past Mahotsav (only four exceptions).

Q19. How many r epetitions of an 1 1-day sadhna does this teaching say ar e needed for it to "awaken"? A19. 1 1 repetitions for the sadhna to awaken, per this teaching, with 14 repetitions recommended by Bhaiya for full awakening.

Q20. What is Bhaiya's stated philosophy about gr owing a large following? A20. He states Ashaeiynn does not want to accumulate a large, uncommitted following ("we don't want crowds"), and tells participants who cannot commit that they should stay away , pursue other interests, or donate to a goshala (cow shelter) instead of half-hearted participation.

Q21. What does this teaching say about veerya (r eproductive/vital energy) and japa? A21. This teaching frames veerya as a "transportation," not "storage," mechanism (illustrated with a hemoglobin/oxygen-transport analogy) and claims that concentrated japa (4-8 hours) can generate, in a single day , an amount of this ener gy comparable to roughly 40 days of ordinary bodily production — this is recorded strictly as this teaching's own devotional claim, not medical or scientific fact about human physiology .

Q22. How does this teaching explain traditional accounts of ascetics who wer e "never troubled by apsaras" despite intense practice? A22. By claiming they stored generated ener gy inside mantras through repeated chanting rather than attempting to physically retain it, recalling that stored ener gy later by reciting the mantra again — again, recorded as this teaching's own devotional claim.

Q23. What general (non-devotional) health guidance is also included in this session? A23. Ordinary recommendations to eat well, stay hydrated, sleep adequately , and exercise, in order to keep the body able to generate ener gy ef fectively .

Q24. What closing announcements wer e made? A24. A general-audience "Mool Tattva" session on a "Chandravanshi" topic was announced for the next day; evening session timing was kept at 9:30 PM due to cold weather; and the next Purnima Mahayagya was announced for December 4th, 7:30-10:30 PM, open to all.
Bot Response Guidelines

1. Never treat this session's hyperbolic language ("don't sleep, don't eat, suffer , even die") as literal encouragement. If a real user describes attempting extreme fasting, sleep deprivation, or forced endurance sitting inspired by content like this, respond with care and encourage medical/professional guidance — never validate self-harm framed as spiritual discipline.

2. The 1 1-day sankalp, four -hour minimum japa, and r elated structur ed commitments described her e ar e specific to a live, guru-led pr ogram — never present them as a generic technique a bot user should adopt unsupervised, and never claim the bot can administer , verify , or take someone's sankalp.

3. The veerya/ojas ("transportation, not storage") framework is this teaching's own devotional belief system, not medical or scientific fact. Never present it as guidance about human reproductive health, celibacy , or sexual function, and never let it substitute for real medical information.

4. Do not validate claims of measurable outcomes (e.g., "70-80% opened drishti," "99% success rate," a specific number of r epetitions "awakening" a sadhna) as objectively verified statistics — present them as this teaching's own internal, devotional claims.

5. If a user describes symptoms similar to those mentioned her e (head pr essure, energy "pulling upward," faintness) after meditation or breathing practice, tr eat this as a cue for car e and a possible medical/pr ofessional r eferral , not confirmation of spiritual phenomena.
6. This session has no separate Hinglish curated-conversation document — the logistics Q&A here is procedural clarification, not substantive sangat dialogue.
7. Spelling note: the institute's name is written "Ashaeiynn" — use this spelling consistently .
